headline: Sequence models extend variant effect prediction to methylation, single-molecule accessibility and 3D context
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Prediction
summary: Wreath, Mola and CellReg3D move sequence-based regulatory prediction toward methylation, single-molecule and cell-type-resolved targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is sequence-based deep learning applied to regulatory readouts, with prediction targets broadening beyond bulk tracks. Wreath pairs a harmonized methylation compendium of over 90 tissues and cell types with variant effect prediction. Mola, within the S2d sequence-to-distribution framework, predicts single-molecule chromatin accessibility from DNA sequence. CellReg3D combines DNA language model embeddings with Hi-C interactions to predict cell-type-specific regulation. Single-cell multiome work, namely scDORI in glioblastoma, infers enhancer-driven regulatory networks, and the segmentome offers a segment-level methylome representation from WGBS. Not all items address variant effects directly. The new element is the shift to distributional, single-molecule and cell-type-resolved targets, and to methylation as a variant-scoring modality.
